scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The 1492 to 1500 imported polygon spans a very broad area. The community source supports a geographically and politically diverse identity, not a single exclusive boundary. Separate Odawa, Potawatomi and Algonquin records are not silently merged into this card.

The card gives regionally located Ojibwe examples and expressly avoids treating every Anishinaabe community as identical. The Three Fires account is attributed to a community education resource without assigning an invented founding year.

The museum’s storage bag is a collected object, not a reported excavation. Its manufacturing interval, collection date, materials and place remain distinct. The bandolier bag has only probable cultural attribution and inferred geographical origin; those qualifications remain visible.

The cradleboard source is a present teaching resource, not an excavation report or proof of a dated origin. No restricted ceremony or unexamined story is reconstructed. Audio recordings were not played.
The late-1950s writing phase is approximate. A shared orthography does not erase dialect variation or mean that Fiero invented the spoken language.

GLIFWC’s rice account describes both customary work and modern materials or mechanization. These are not all projected into the year 1492. Monitoring information does not substitute for individual tribal harvesting rules.

The community treaty interpretation and the Supreme Court’s legal terminology differ and are attributed. The community teaching page gives an older 1874 payment date, while the judgment specifically documents the 1875 increase; only the latter is used for chronology.

Restoule is described as a 2024 historical ruling. No assertion is made about full implementation, later payment totals, or individual entitlement today. The source URL points to the judgment, whose indexed text and case summary were consulted.
The 2022 agreement applied to its named signatory nations and specified governance areas. It is not described as extinguishing the Indian Act everywhere or representing every Anishinaabe nation.
No sourced phase is artificially assigned to the narrow 1492 to 1500 map interval. No single conquest year, extinct-people claim or unverified successor link is supplied.
Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
